title.zh: 卷一百十一 列傳第六十一: 崔光遠 房琯 張鎬 高適 暢璀
title.en: Volume 111 Biographies 61: Cui Guan Yuan, Fang Guan, Zhang Gao, Gao Shi, Chang Cui
title.raw: 卷一百十一 列傳第六十一: 崔光遠 房琯 張鎬 高適 暢璀 Volume 111 Biographies 61: Cui Guan Yuan, Fang Guan, Zhang Gao, Gao Shi, Chang Cui

sentences.zh: 崔光遠，滑州靈昌人也。

translations.literal: Cui Guangyuan was a native of Lingchang in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guangyuan came from Lingchang in Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 本博陵舊族。

translations.literal: His clan was originally of the old Boling aristocracy.
translations.idiomatic: He was descended from the old Boling aristocracy.

sentences.zh: 祖敬嗣，好樗蒱飲酒。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jingsi loved playing chuck-a-luck and drinking wine.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jingsi was fond of gambling at chuck-a-luck and of wine.

sentences.zh: 則天初，為房州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Empress Wu's reign, he served as prefect of Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the early years of Empress Wu, he served as prefect of Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 中宗為廬陵王，安置在州，官吏多無禮度，敬嗣獨以親賢待之，供給豐贍，中宗深德之。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was Prince of Luling and was placed in that prefecture, most officials showed him no proper courtesy; Jingsi alone treated him with the affection due a kinsman and worthy, supplied him generously, and Zhongzong was deeply grateful.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was Prince of Luling and was kept at Fangzhou, most officials treated him without proper respect; only Jingsi received him as kin and as a man of worth and provided for him lavishly, and Zhongzong never forgot his kindness.

sentences.zh: 及登位，有益州長史崔敬嗣，既同姓名，每進擬官，皆御筆超拜之者數四。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong ascended the throne, there was a Yizhou chief administrator named Cui Jingsi who bore the same name; whenever proposed appointments were submitted, the emperor four times used his own brush to promote him beyond the normal rank.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongzong took the throne, a chief administrator of Yizhou named Cui Jingsi shared the same name, and on four separate occasions when appointments were proposed the emperor personally marked him for extraordinary promotion.

sentences.zh: 後引與語，始知誤寵。

translations.literal: Later he summoned the man to speak with him and only then realized he had favored the wrong man.
translations.idiomatic: Only when he later summoned the man to court did he discover his mistake.

sentences.zh: 訪敬嗣已卒，乃遣中書令韋安石授其子汪官。

translations.literal: Learning that Jingsi had already died, he sent Chief Minister Wei Anshi to confer an office on his son Wang.
translations.idiomatic: On learning that Jingsi was dead, he sent Chief Minister Wei Anshi to grant an office to his son Wang.

sentences.zh: 汪嗜酒不堪職任，且授洛州司功，又改五品。

translations.literal: Wang was addicted to wine and unfit for office; he was therefore given the post of Registrar of Luozhou, then reduced to fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wang drank heavily and could not hold office, so he was first made Registrar of Luozhou and later demoted to fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 光遠即汪之子，雖無學術，頗有祖風，勇決任氣，身長六尺余，目睛白黑分明。

translations.literal: Guangyuan was Wang's son; though he had little learning, he showed something of his grandfather's spirit—bold, decisive, and headstrong—stood more than six feet tall, and his eyes were strikingly clear between white and black.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan was Wang's son. He lacked scholarship but had something of his grandfather's temper: bold, impulsive, and over six feet tall, with eyes whose whites and pupils were sharply defined.

sentences.zh: 少歷仕州縣。

translations.literal: In his youth he served in succession in prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he held posts in one prefecture and county after another.

sentences.zh: 開元末為蜀州唐安令，與楊國忠以博徒相得，累遷至左贊善大夫。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he was magistrate of Tang'an in Shu Prefecture; he and Yang Guozhong became friends as fellow gamblers, and he rose in stages to Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Kaiyuan period he was magistrate of Tang'an in Shuzhou, became close to Yang Guozhong through gambling, and was promoted step by step to Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 天寶十一載，京兆尹鮮于仲通舉光遠為長安令。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianbao, Metropolitan Governor Xianyu Zhongtong recommended Guangyuan as magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao year 11, Metropolitan Governor Xianyu Zhongtong recommended Guangyuan as magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 十四載，遷京兆少尹。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Metropolitan Vice Governor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he became Metropolitan Vice Governor.

sentences.zh: 其載，使吐蕃吊祭。

translations.literal: That year he was sent to Tibet on a mourning mission.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was dispatched to Tibet for condolence rites.

sentences.zh: 十五載五月，使回。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifteenth year he returned from his mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 15 he returned from his mission.

sentences.zh: 十余日，潼關失守，玄宗幸蜀，詔留光遠為京兆尹、兼御史中丞，充西京留守采訪使。

translations.literal: More than ten days later Tong Pass fell, Emperor Xuanzong fled to Shu, and an edict left Guangyuan as Metropolitan Governor, also Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Western Capital garrison commissioner and investigation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Ten-odd days later, after Tong Pass was lost and Xuanzong fled toward Shu, Guangyuan was ordered to remain as Metropolitan Governor and Vice Censor-in-Chief and to serve as garrison and investigation commissioner for the western capital.

sentences.zh: 駕發，百姓亂入宮禁，取左藏大盈庫物，既而焚之，自旦及午，火勢漸盛，亦有乘驢上紫宸、興慶殿者。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage departed, the common people broke into the palace precincts, looted the Left Storehouse and the Great Abundance Treasury, and then set fires; from dawn until noon the blaze spread, and some even rode donkeys up to the Zichen and Xingqing halls.
translations.idiomatic: As the court left the city, crowds stormed the palace, stripped the Left Storehouse and Great Abundance Treasury, and set them ablaze; from morning until midday the fire grew, and some rode donkeys onto the Zichen and Xingqing palace halls.

sentences.zh: 光遠與中官將軍邊令誠號令百姓救火，又募人攝府縣官分守之，殺十數人方定。

translations.literal: Guangyuan, together with the eunuch general Bian Lingcheng, ordered the people to fight the fire, also recruited men to act temporarily as prefectural and county officials to guard districts, and killed more than ten men before order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan and the eunuch general Bian Lingcheng directed the populace to fight the fire, appointed temporary prefectural and county officers to hold districts, and had more than a dozen men executed before calm returned.

sentences.zh: 使其息東見祿山，祿山大悅，偽敕復本官。

translations.literal: He sent his son Dong to see An Lushan; Lushan was greatly pleased and issued a forged edict restoring him to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his son Dong to An Lushan, who was delighted and issued a forged edict restoring Guangyuan to his former post.

sentences.zh: 先是祿山已令張休攝京兆尹十余日，既得光遠歸款，召休歸洛。

translations.literal: Earlier Lushan had already had Zhang Xiu act as Metropolitan Governor for more than ten days; once Guangyuan submitted, Xiu was recalled to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan had already placed Zhang Xiu in charge of the metropolitan government for over ten days; when Guangyuan came over, Xiu was summoned back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 八月，同羅背祿山，以廄馬二千出至浐水。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Tongluo turned against Lushan and drove two thousand stable horses out to Chan River.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Tongluo rebelled against Lushan and drove two thousand imperial horses out toward Chan River.

sentences.zh: 孫孝哲、安神威從而召之，不得，神威懼而憂死，府縣官吏驚走，獄囚皆空。

translations.literal: Sun Xiaozhe and An Shenwei went to summon them but failed; Shenwei died of fear, prefectural and county officials fled in panic, and the prisons were emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiaozhe and An Shenwei went to recall them without success; Shenwei died of fright, officials fled, and the jails were emptied.

sentences.zh: 光遠以為賊且逃矣，命所由守神威孝哲宅。

translations.literal: Guangyuan thought the rebels were about to flee and ordered subordinates to guard the residences of Shenwei and Xiaozhe.
translations.idiomatic: Believing the rebels were about to run, Guangyuan ordered men to guard Shenwei's and Xiaozhe's houses.

sentences.zh: 孝哲以光遠之狀報祿山。

translations.literal: Xiaozhe reported Guangyuan's conduct to Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhe reported Guangyuan's actions to Lushan.

sentences.zh: 光遠閉府門，斬為盜曳落河二人，遂與長安令蘇震等同出。

translations.literal: Guangyuan shut the government offices, beheaded two robbers who were called yeluohe, and then left together with Metropolitan Magistrate Su Zhen and others.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan closed the yamen, executed two robbers called yeluohe, and fled with Metropolitan Magistrate Su Zhen and others.

sentences.zh: 至開遠門，使人前謂門官曰：「尹巡諸門。」

translations.literal: At Kaiyuan Gate he sent a man ahead to tell the gate officers, "The governor is inspecting the gates."
translations.idiomatic: At Kaiyuan Gate he sent someone ahead to say, "The metropolitan governor is making his rounds of the gates."

sentences.zh: 門官具器仗以迎，至則皆斬之。

translations.literal: The gate officers prepared arms to receive him, and when he arrived he had them all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The gate guards armed themselves to welcome him—and he had every one of them killed.

sentences.zh: 領府縣官十余人，於京西號令百姓，赴召者百余人，夜過咸陽，遂達靈武。

translations.literal: Leading more than ten prefectural and county officials, he rallied the people west of the capital; over a hundred answered his call, passed Xianyang by night, and reached Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: With a dozen prefectural and county officials he rallied people west of the capital; more than a hundred joined him, crossed Xianyang by night, and reached Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 上喜之，擢拜御史大夫，兼京兆尹，仍使光遠於渭北召集人吏之歸順者。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, promoted him to Censor-in-Chief and Metropolitan Governor, and still had Guangyuan gather on the north bank of the Wei those officials and people who had submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, made him Censor-in-Chief and Metropolitan Governor, and sent him north of the Wei to gather officials and commoners who had come over.

sentences.zh: 嘗有賊剽掠涇陽縣界，於僧寺中椎牛釃酒，連夜酣飲，去光遠營四十里。

translations.literal: Once bandits plundered the border of Jingyang County, slaughtered an ox and poured wine in a monastery, and drank through the night; they were forty li from Guangyuan's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits once raided Jingyang County, butchered an ox and poured wine in a temple, and caroused all night forty li from Guangyuan's camp.

sentences.zh: 光遠偵知之，率馬步二千乙夜趨其所。

translations.literal: Guangyuan learned of it by reconnaissance and led two thousand horse and foot in the second watch to their position.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan learned of it through scouts and at the second watch led two thousand horse and foot to the spot.

sentences.zh: 賊徒多醉，光遠領百余騎持滿扼其要，分命驍勇持陌刀呼而斬之，殺賊徒二千余人，虜馬千疋，俘其渠酋一人。

translations.literal: Most of the bandits were drunk; Guangyuan led a hundred-odd horsemen with bows drawn to block the vital point, ordered fierce men with broad blades to shout and cut them down, killed more than two thousand bandits, captured a thousand horses, and took one chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Most were drunk. Guangyuan took a hundred-odd mounted archers to hold the choke point, sent picked men with broad blades to cut them down, killed over two thousand, seized a thousand horses, and captured one chieftain.

sentences.zh: 賊中以光遠勇勁，常避其鋒。

translations.literal: Among the rebels Guangyuan was known for fierceness, and they usually avoided his edge.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels knew him for ferocity and generally kept clear of him.

sentences.zh: 及扈從還京，論功行賞，制曰：「持節京畿采訪、計會、招召、宣慰、處置等使崔光遠，毀家成國，致命前茅。

translations.literal: When he returned to the capital with the emperor, rewards were granted for merit; the edict said, "Cui Guangyuan, commissioner with full powers for metropolitan investigation, accounting, recruitment, consolation, and disposition, ruined his household to serve the state and risked his life at the front.
translations.idiomatic: On the return to Chang'an, an edict praised "Cui Guangyuan, commissioner for metropolitan investigation, accounting, recruitment, consolation, and disposition, who ruined his household for the state and staked his life at the van.

sentences.zh: 可特進，行禮部尚書，封鄴國公，食實封三百戶。」

translations.literal: He may be made Special Advancement, acting Minister of Rites, enfeoffed Duke of Ye with three hundred households of actual fief."
translations.idiomatic: He was to receive Special Advancement, act as Minister of Rites, and be enfeoffed Duke of Ye with three hundred households of substantive fief."

sentences.zh: 乾元元年，兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan he also held the post of Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan 1 he also served as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 五月，為河南節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he became military commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he became Henan military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 八月，代張鎬為汴州刺史，兼本州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he replaced Zhang Gao as prefect of Bianzhou and also defense commissioner of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he replaced Zhang Gao as prefect of Bianzhou and defense commissioner of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十二月，代蕭華為魏州刺史，充魏州節度使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he replaced Xiao Hua as prefect of Weizhou and military commissioner of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he replaced Xiao Hua as prefect of Weizhou and military commissioner of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，司徒郭子儀與賊戰於汲郡，光遠率汴師千人渡河援之。

translations.literal: Earlier Grand Marshal Guo Ziyi had fought the rebels at Ji Commandery, and Guangyuan led a thousand Bian troops across the river to reinforce him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Grand Marshal Guo Ziyi had fought rebels at Ji, and Guangyuan led a thousand Bian troops across the river to aid him.

sentences.zh: 及代蕭華入魏州，使將軍李處崟拒賊，賊大至，連戰不利，子儀怒不救，處崟遂敗，奔還。

translations.literal: When he entered Weizhou in place of Xiao Hua he sent General Li Chuyin to hold off the rebels; the rebels came in force, battles went badly, Ziyi angrily refused rescue, Chuyin was defeated and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: After replacing Xiao Hua at Weizhou he sent General Li Chuyin against the rebels; they came in strength, fighting went poorly, Ziyi in anger would not help, and Chuyin was beaten and fled back.

sentences.zh: 賊逐處崟至城下，反問之曰：「處崟召我來，何為不出？」

translations.literal: The rebels pursued Chuyin to the foot of the wall and shouted up, "Chuyin summoned us—why do you not come out?"
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing Chuyin to the walls, the rebels shouted, "Chuyin called us here—why won't you come out?"

sentences.zh: 光遠乃腰斬處崟。

translations.literal: Guangyuan then cut Chuyin in two at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan had Chuyin cut in two at the waist.

sentences.zh: 處崟善戰有勇，眾皆倚之，及死，人用危懼。

translations.literal: Chuyin was skilled in battle and brave; the troops all relied on him, and when he died the men were filled with dread.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyin was a capable, brave fighter whom the army trusted; after his death the men were terrified.

sentences.zh: 魏州城自祿山反，袁知泰、能元皓等皆繕完之，甚為堅峻。

translations.literal: Since Lushan's rebellion Yuan Zhita and Neng Yuanhao and others had repaired Weizhou's walls, which were very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Since Lushan's revolt Yuan Zhita, Neng Yuanhao, and others had repaired Weizhou until its defenses were very strong.

sentences.zh: 光遠不能守，遂夜潰圍而出，度河而還。

translations.literal: Guangyuan could not hold it, broke out of the encirclement by night, crossed the river, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to hold the city, he broke out at night, crossed the river, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 肅宗不之罪，除太子少保。

translations.literal: Suzong did not punish him and appointed him Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong did not punish him and made him Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 襄州將士康楚元、張嘉延率眾為亂，陷荊、襄、澧、朗等州，以光遠兼御史大夫，持節荊襄招討，仍充山南東道處置兵馬都使。

translations.literal: Xiangzhou officers and soldiers Kang Chuyuan and Zhang Jiayan led the masses in rebellion, seized Jing, Xiang, Li, Lang, and other prefectures, and Guangyuan was made Censor-in-Chief with full powers as pacification commissioner of Jing and Xiang and still served as overall commander of armies for the Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Chuyuan and Zhang Jiayan of Xiangzhou rebelled and seized Jing, Xiang, Li, Lang, and other prefectures. Guangyuan was made Censor-in-Chief with full powers to pacify Jing and Xiang and still served as overall commander of Shannan East Circuit forces.

sentences.zh: 三年，除鳳翔尹，充本府及秦隴觀察使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made metropolitan governor of Fengxiang and observation commissioner of that prefecture and of Qin and Long.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became Fengxiang metropolitan governor and observation commissioner of Fengxiang and of Qin and Long.

sentences.zh: 先是，岐、隴吏人郭愔等為土賊，掠州縣，為五堡，光遠使判官、監察御史嚴侁召而降之。

translations.literal: Earlier Guo Yin and other local men of Qi and Long had become bandits, plundered prefectures and counties, and built five forts; Guangyuan sent his aide and investigating censor Yan Shen to summon and accept their surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Guo Yin and other local bandits in Qi and Long had raided the region and built five forts. Guangyuan sent his aide and investigating censor Yan Shen to summon them and accept their surrender.

sentences.zh: 光遠在官好蒱酒，晚年不親戎事。

translations.literal: While in office Guangyuan loved dice and wine, and in his later years he did not personally attend to military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In office Guangyuan loved gambling and wine, and in later years he no longer personally commanded troops.

sentences.zh: 上元元年冬，愔等潛連黨項及奴剌、突厥敗韋倫於秦、隴，殺監軍使，擊黃戍。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Shangyuan, Yin and the rest secretly joined the Tangut, Nula, and Turks, defeated Wei Lun at Qin and Long, killed the army supervisor, and attacked Huang Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Shangyuan 1, Yin secretly allied with Tangut, Nula, and Turkic forces, defeated Wei Lun in Qin and Long, killed the army supervisor, and attacked Huang Fort.

sentences.zh: 肅宗追還，以李鼎代之。

translations.literal: Suzong recalled him and sent Li Ding to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong recalled him and replaced him with Li Ding.

sentences.zh: 二年，兼成都尹，充劍南節度營田觀察處置使，仍兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year he also became metropolitan governor of Chengdu, military commissioner of Jiannan for farming colonies, observation, and disposition, and still held Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he also became Chengdu metropolitan governor and Jiannan military commissioner for farming colonies, observation, and disposition, while retaining the post of Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 及段子璋反，東川節度使李奐敗走，投光遠，率將花驚定等討平之。

translations.literal: When Duan Zizhang rebelled, Dongchuan military commissioner Li Huan was defeated and fled, threw himself on Guangyuan, and Guangyuan led generals including Hua Jingding to suppress and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Zizhang rebelled, Dongchuan commissioner Li Huan was beaten and fled to Guangyuan, who led generals including Hua Jingding to put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 將士肆其剽劫，婦女有金銀臂釧，兵士皆斷其腕以取之，亂殺數千人，光遠不能禁。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers indulged in plunder; when women wore gold and silver bracelets the soldiers cut off their wrists to take them, wantonly killing several thousand people, and Guangyuan could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: His troops looted freely; soldiers cut off women's wrists to seize gold and silver bracelets and killed thousands in the chaos, and Guangyuan could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 肅宗遣監軍官使按其罪，光遠憂恚成疾，上元二年十月卒。

translations.literal: Suzong sent a supervising army official to investigate his guilt; Guangyuan fell ill from anxiety and resentment and died in the tenth month of the second year of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong sent a supervising army official to investigate him. Guangyuan fell ill from anxiety and died in the tenth month of Shangyuan 2.

sentences.zh: 房琯，河南人，天後朝正議大夫、平章事融之子也。

translations.literal: Fang Guan was a man of Henan, son of Zheng Yilang Grandee and Grand Councillor Rong of the Empress Wu era.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guan, a native of Henan, was the son of Zheng Yilang Grandee and Grand Councillor Rong from Empress Wu's court.

sentences.zh: 琯少好學，風儀沈整，以門廕補弘文生。

translations.literal: Guan studied diligently in youth, his bearing grave and composed; by hereditary privilege he entered the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Guan loved learning and bore himself with grave composure; by yin privilege he entered the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 性好隱遁，與東平呂向於陸渾伊陽山中讀書為事，凡十余歲。

translations.literal: By nature he loved seclusion; with Lü Xiang of Dongping he spent more than ten years reading in the mountains of Luhun and Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was drawn to reclusion and spent more than ten years in the Luhun and Yiyang mountains reading with Lü Xiang of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 開元十二年，玄宗將封岱嶽，琯撰《封禪書》一篇及箋啟以獻。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan 12, as Xuanzong prepared to perform the Feng and Shan rites at Mount Tai, Guan submitted his 《Fengshan Shu》 and memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 12, as Xuanzong prepared to perform the Feng and Shan rites at Mount Tai, Guan submitted his 《Fengshan Shu》 and memorials.

sentences.zh: 中書令張說奇其才，奏授秘書省校書郎，調補同州馮翊尉。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Yue marveled at his talent, memorialized appointment as collator in the Secretariat, and he was transferred to fill the post of Wei of Fengyi in Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Yue admired his talent, had him appointed collator in the Secretariat, and transferred him to be Wei of Fengyi in Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 無幾去官，應堪任縣令舉，授虢州盧氏令，政多惠愛，人稱美之。

translations.literal: Before long he left office; answering the recommendation for men fit to be county magistrates, he was made magistrate of Lushi in Guo Prefecture, his administration full of kindness, and the people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he resigned; recommended as fit for county magistrate, he was made magistrate of Lushi in Guozhou, governed with kindness, and won praise.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 he was made investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 其年坐鞫獄不當，貶睦州司戶。

translations.literal: That year for improper conduct in trying cases he was demoted to Registrar of Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year, for mishandling a trial, he was demoted to Registrar of Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 歷慈溪、宋城、濟源縣令，所在為政，多興利除害，繕理廨宇，頗著能名。

translations.literal: He served in succession as magistrate of Cixi, Songcheng, and Jiyuan; wherever he governed he promoted benefit and removed harm, repaired government buildings, and won a name for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Cixi, Songcheng, and Jiyuan in turn; everywhere he promoted public good, removed abuses, repaired yamens, and gained a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年，拜主客員外郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao he was appointed vice director of the Bureau of Receptions.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 1 he was made vice director of the Bureau of Receptions.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷試主客郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to acting director of the Bureau of Receptions.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he became acting director of the Bureau of Receptions.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，擢試給事中，賜爵漳南縣男。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year he was promoted to acting supervising secretary and enfeoffed Baron of Zhangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 5 he was promoted to acting supervising secretary and enfeoffed Baron of Zhangnan.

sentences.zh: 時玄宗企慕古道，數遊幸近甸，乃分新豐縣置會昌縣於驪山下，尋改會昌為昭應縣，又改溫泉宮為華清宮，於宮所立百司廨舍。

translations.literal: At that time Xuanzong admired the ancient way and often toured the nearby suburbs; he divided Xinfeng County to establish Huichang County at Mount Li, soon changed Huichang to Zhaoying, changed the Hot Spring Palace to Huaqing Palace, and built offices for the hundred bureaus at the palace site.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong then admired antiquity and often visited the suburbs near the capital; he split off Huichang from Xinfeng below Mount Li, renamed it Zhaoying, turned the Hot Spring Palace into Huaqing Palace, and built offices for the hundred bureaus there.

sentences.zh: 以琯雅有巧思，令充使繕理。

translations.literal: Because Guan was known for elegant ingenuity, he was made commissioner to oversee the work.
translations.idiomatic: Because Guan was known for elegant ingenuity, he was put in charge of the construction.

sentences.zh: 事未畢，坐與李適之、韋堅等善，貶宜春太守。

translations.literal: Before the work was finished, for association with Li Shizhi, Wei Jian, and others he was demoted to prefect of Yichun.
translations.idiomatic: Before the work was finished, association with Li Shizhi and Wei Jian brought demotion to prefect of Yichun.

sentences.zh: 歷瑯邪、鄴郡、扶風三太守，所至多有遺愛。

translations.literal: He served in succession as prefect of Langye, Ye Commandery, and Fufeng; wherever he went he left enduring kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He then governed Langye, Ye, and Fufeng in succession, leaving affection wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 十四年，征拜左庶子，遷憲部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was summoned as Left Subordinate of the Heir Apparent and transferred to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he was summoned as Left Subordinate of the Heir Apparent and made Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 十五年六月，玄宗蒼黃幸蜀，大臣陳希烈、張倚等銜於失恩，不時赴難。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year Xuanzong fled in haste to Shu; grandees Chen Xilie and Zhang Yi and others, resentful at lost favor, did not hurry to the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year 15 Xuanzong fled in panic to Shu; ministers Chen Xilie and Zhang Yi, bitter over lost favor, did not hurry to his side.

sentences.zh: 琯結張均、張垍兄弟與韋述等行至城南十數里山寺，均、垍同行，皆以家在城中，逗留不進，琯獨馳蜀路。

translations.literal: Guan joined Zhang Jun and Zhang Ya and brothers with Wei Shu and others and went to a mountain temple ten-odd li south of the city; Jun and Ya, whose families were in the city, lingered and would not advance, but Guan alone galloped along the road to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Guan joined Zhang Jun and Zhang Ya with Wei Shu and reached a mountain temple south of the city; the Zhang brothers, with kin in the capital, hung back, while Guan alone raced toward Shu.

sentences.zh: 七月，至普安郡謁見，玄宗大悅，即日拜文部尚書、同中書門下平章事，賜紫金魚袋。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he presented himself at Pu'an Commandery; Xuanzong was greatly pleased and that same day appointed him Minister of Culture, Grand Councillor with the Secretariat, and granted the gold and purple fish bag.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he presented himself at Pu'an; Xuanzong was delighted and that day made him Minister of Culture, Grand Councillor, and gave him the gold-and-purple fish bag.

sentences.zh: 從幸成都，加銀青光祿大夫，仍與一子官。

translations.literal: Following the court to Chengdu, he was given the silver and blue glory grandee rank and an office for one son.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the court to Chengdu, received Silver and Blue Glory Grandee rank, and an office for one son.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，與左相韋見素、門下侍郎崔渙等奉使靈武，冊立肅宗。

translations.literal: That eighth month, with Left Chancellor Wei Jiansu and Vice Director of the Secretariat Cui Huan and others, he was sent as envoy to Lingwu to invest Suzong.
translations.idiomatic: That eighth month, with Left Chancellor Wei Jiansu and Vice Director Cui Huan, he went to Lingwu to invest Suzong.

sentences.zh: 至順化郡謁見，陳上皇傳付之旨，因言時事，詞情慷慨，肅宗為之改容。

translations.literal: Presenting himself at Shunhua Commandery, he declared the retired emperor's transmitted charge and spoke on current affairs with passionate words; Suzong's expression changed.
translations.idiomatic: At Shunhua he delivered the retired emperor's charge and spoke on affairs of the day with passion, and Suzong's face changed.

sentences.zh: 時潼關敗將王思禮、呂崇賁、李承光等引於纛下，將斬之，琯從容救諫，獨斬承光而已。

translations.literal: At that time the defeated generals from Tong Pass—Wang Sili, Lü Chongben, Li Chengguang, and others—were brought before the banners to be executed; Guan calmly remonstrated and only Chengguang was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated Tong Pass generals Wang Sili, Lü Chongben, and Li Chengguang were brought to the standards for execution; Guan calmly argued them down, and only Chengguang was killed.

sentences.zh: 肅宗以琯素有重名，傾意待之，琯亦自負其才，以天下為己任。

translations.literal: Suzong, because Guan had long enjoyed a great reputation, treated him with full favor; Guan too relied on his talent and took the empire as his charge.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong, knowing Guan's long-standing fame, favored him wholeheartedly; Guan in turn trusted his own gifts and took the realm as his responsibility.

sentences.zh: 時行在機務，多決之於琯，凡有大事，諸將無敢預言。

translations.literal: At the mobile court most business was decided by Guan; on great matters the generals did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: At the mobile court most affairs were settled by Guan; on major matters the generals hardly dared speak.

sentences.zh: 尋抗疏自請將兵以誅寇孽，收復京都，肅宗望其成功，許之。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized asking to lead troops to destroy the rebels and recover the capital; Suzong hoped for success and assented.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked in a memorial to lead troops against the rebels and recover the capital; Suzong hoped he would succeed and agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔加持節、招討西京兼防禦蒲潼兩關兵馬節度等使，乃與子儀、光弼等計會進兵。

translations.literal: An edict added full powers as commissioner to reconnoiter the western capital and defend the armies of Pu and Tong passes, and he consulted with Ziyi, Guangbi, and others on advancing.
translations.idiomatic: He was given full powers to reconnoiter the western capital and command the Pu and Tong garrisons, and planned advances with Ziyi and Guangbi.

sentences.zh: 琯請自選參佐，乃以禦中史中丞鄧景山為副，戶部侍郎李揖為行軍司馬，中丞宋若思、起居郎知制誥賈至、右司郎中魏少遊為判官，給事中劉秩為參謀。

translations.literal: Guan asked to choose his own staff: Vice Censor-in-Chief Deng Jingshan as deputy, Vice Minister of Revenue Li Yi as army marshal, censors Song Ruosi and Jia Zhi and Right Department Director Wei Shaoyou as judges, and supervising secretary Liu Zhi as staff adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Guan chose his staff: Vice Censor-in-Chief Deng Jingshan as deputy, Vice Minister Li Yi as army marshal, Song Ruosi, Jia Zhi, and Wei Shaoyou as judges, and Liu Zhi as adviser.

sentences.zh: 既行，又令兵部尚書王思禮副之。

translations.literal: After setting out, Minister of War Wang Sili was also made his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: After he marched, Minister of War Wang Sili was added as deputy.

sentences.zh: 琯分為三軍：遣楊希文將南軍，自宜壽入；

translations.literal: Guan divided into three armies: Yang Xiwen was to lead the southern army in from Yishou;
translations.idiomatic: Guan divided his force: Yang Xiwen would lead the southern army in from Yishou;

sentences.zh: 劉悊將中軍，自武功入；

translations.literal: Liu Ti was to lead the central army in from Wugong;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ti the central army from Wugong;

sentences.zh: 李光進將北軍，自奉天入。

translations.literal: Li Guangjin was to lead the northern army in from Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangjin the northern army from Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 琯自將中軍，為前鋒。

translations.literal: Guan himself led the central army as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Guan himself commanded the central army as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 十月庚子，師次便橋。

translations.literal: On the gengzi day of the tenth month the army halted at Bian Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi in the tenth month the army camped at Bian Bridge.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，二軍先遇賊於咸陽縣之陳濤斜，接戰，官軍敗績。

translations.literal: On xinchou the two armies first met the rebels at Chentaoxie in Xianyang County; they joined battle and the government troops were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou two armies met the rebels at Chentaoxie in Xianyang and were routed.

sentences.zh: 時琯用春秋車戰之法，以車二千乘，馬步夾之。

translations.literal: At that time Guan used Spring and Autumn chariot warfare, with two thousand chariots and horse and foot on either side.
translations.idiomatic: Guan fought by Spring and Autumn chariot rules, with two thousand chariots flanked by infantry and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 既戰，賊順風揚塵鼓噪，牛皆震駭，因縛芻縱火焚之，人畜撓敗，為所傷殺者四萬余人，存者數千而已。

translations.literal: Once battle was joined the rebels, with the wind at their backs, raised dust and shouted; the oxen were terrified, fodder was bound and set afire, men and beasts were thrown into chaos, more than forty thousand were killed or wounded, and only a few thousand survived.
translations.idiomatic: In battle the rebels, wind at their backs, raised dust and clamor; oxen panicked, fodder was fired, men and beasts broke, more than forty thousand were killed or hurt, and only thousands remained.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，琯又率南軍即戰，復敗，希文、劉悊並降於賊。

translations.literal: On guimao Guan again led the southern army into battle, was again defeated, and Xiwen and Liu Ti both surrendered to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Guan led the southern army again, lost again, and Xiwen and Liu Ti surrendered.

sentences.zh: 琯等奔赴行在，肉袒請罪，上並宥之。

translations.literal: Guan and the others ran to the mobile court, bared their torsos to ask punishment, and the emperor pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Guan and his party rushed to the mobile court, stripped to the waist to beg punishment, and were all pardoned.

sentences.zh: 琯好賓客，喜談論，用兵素非所長，而天子采其虛聲，冀成實效。

translations.literal: Guan loved guests and discussion; military affairs were never his strength, yet the Son of Heaven took his empty reputation and hoped for real results.
translations.idiomatic: Guan loved guests and talk; war was never his strength, yet the emperor seized on his name and hoped for deeds.

sentences.zh: 琯既自無廟勝，又以虛名擇將吏，以至於敗。

translations.literal: Guan himself had no winning plan in the temple and chose officers by empty reputation, and so came to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He had no strategy and picked commanders for reputation alone—and so he fell.

sentences.zh: 琯之出師，戎務一委於李揖、劉秩，秩等亦儒家子，未嘗習軍旅之事。

translations.literal: When Guan took the field he left all military affairs to Li Yi and Liu Zhi; Zhi and the rest were also Confucian sons who had never studied campaigning.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he left war to Li Yi and Liu Zhi, Confucian scholars who had never soldiered.

sentences.zh: 琯臨戎謂人曰：「逆黨曳落河雖多，豈能當我劉秩等？」

translations.literal: Facing the enemy Guan told others, "Though the rebel yeluohe are many, how can they stand against my Liu Zhi and the rest?"
translations.idiomatic: Before battle he said, "However many rebel yeluohe there are, can they match my Liu Zhi?"

sentences.zh: 及與賊對壘，琯欲持重以伺之，為中使邢延恩等督戰，蒼黃失據，遂及於敗。

translations.literal: When he faced the rebel camps he wished to wait cautiously, but eunuch Xing Yan'en and others pressed for battle; in panic he lost his footing and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Facing the enemy he wanted to wait, but eunuchs such as Xing Yan'en forced action; he lost his footing and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 上猶待之如初，仍令收合散卒，更圖進取。

translations.literal: The emperor still treated him as before and ordered him to gather scattered troops and plan another advance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still treated him as before and told him to regather troops and try again.

sentences.zh: 會北海太守賀蘭進明自河南至，詔授南海太守，攝御史大夫，充嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: When Beihai Prefect Helan Jinming came from Henan, an edict made him prefect of Nanhai, acting Censor-in-Chief, and military commissioner of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Beihai Prefect Helan Jinming arrived from Henan, an edict made him Nanhai prefect, acting Censor-in-Chief, and Lingnan commissioner.

sentences.zh: 中謝，肅宗謂之曰：「朕處分房琯與卿正大夫，何為攝也？」

translations.literal: At court thanks Suzong said to him, "I assigned Fang Guan and you as chief ministers—why are you only acting?"
translations.idiomatic: At thanksgiving audience Suzong said, "I made Fang Guan and you chief ministers—why are you only acting?"

sentences.zh: 進明對曰：「琯與臣有隙。」

translations.literal: Jinming replied, "Guan and I are at odds."
translations.idiomatic: Jinming answered, "Guan and I are at odds."

sentences.zh: 上以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this reasonable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought that plausible.

sentences.zh: 進明因奏曰：「陛下知晉朝何以至亂？」

translations.literal: Jinming then memorialized, "Does Your Majesty know why the Jin dynasty fell into chaos?"
translations.idiomatic: Jinming then asked, "Does Your Majesty know why the Jin fell into chaos?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿有說乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Do you have an explanation?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What is your view?"

sentences.zh: 進明曰：「晉朝以好尚虛名，任王夷甫為宰相，祖習浮華，故至於敗。

translations.literal: Jinming said, "The Jin dynasty honored empty reputation, made Wang Yifu grand councillor, and inherited flashy habits, and so came to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Jinming said, "The Jin honored empty fame, put Wang Yifu in the chancellery, and clung to flashy habits until the state collapsed.

sentences.zh: 今陛下方興復社稷，當委用實才，而琯性疏闊，徒大言耳，非宰相器也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty is restoring the altars of state and should employ men of real ability; Guan is by nature broad and careless, only big talk, and not material for grand councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty is reviving the realm and should use real talent; Guan is loose and grandiloquent—not chancellor timber.

sentences.zh: 陛下待琯至厚，以臣觀之，琯終不為陛下用。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty treats Guan very generously, but in my view Guan will never serve Your Majesty faithfully."
translations.idiomatic: You treat Guan lavishly, yet I do not believe he will ever serve you faithfully."

sentences.zh: 上問其故，進明曰：「琯昨於南朝為聖皇制置天下，乃以永王為江南節度，潁王為劍南節度，盛王為淮南節度，制雲『命元子北略朔方，命諸王分守重鎮』。

translations.literal: The emperor asked why; Jinming said, "When Guan was at the southern court arranging the realm for the Retired Emperor, he made Prince Yong Jiangnan commissioner, Prince Ying Jiannan commissioner, Prince Sheng Huainan commissioner, and the edict read, 'Order the Eldest Son to march north on Shuofang and order the princes each to hold a key post.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, Jinming said that at the southern court Guan had made Prince Yong Jiangnan commissioner, Prince Ying Jiannan commissioner, Prince Sheng Huainan commissioner, and written that the heir should march north while every prince held a great fief.

sentences.zh: 且太子出為撫軍，入曰監國，琯乃以枝庶悉領大籓，皇儲反居邊鄙，此雖於聖皇似忠，於陛下非忠也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the crown prince goes out he is styled commander and when he enters he is styled regent; Guan had the collateral princes all hold great fiefs while the imperial heir sat on the frontier—loyal to the Retired Emperor perhaps, but not to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The heir goes out as commander and in as regent; Guan gave every collateral prince a great post and left the heir on the border—perhaps loyal to the retired emperor, but not to you.

sentences.zh: 琯立此意，以為聖皇諸子，但一人得天下，即不失恩寵。

translations.literal: Guan set up this design thinking that among the Retired Emperor's sons, if only one won the realm he would not lose favor.
translations.idiomatic: His plan assumed that among the retired emperor's sons, whoever won the throne would still favor him.

sentences.zh: 又各樹其私黨劉秩、李揖、劉匯、鄧景山、竇紹之徒，以副戎權。

translations.literal: He also planted private factions—Liu Zhi, Li Yi, Liu Hui, Deng Jingshan, Dou Shao, and the like—to share military power.
translations.idiomatic: He planted private men—Liu Zhi, Li Yi, Liu Hui, Deng Jingshan, Dou Shao—to share command.

sentences.zh: 推此而言，琯豈肯盡誠於陛下乎？

translations.literal: Pushing this reasoning, would Guan devote himself wholly to Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: By that logic, would he ever give you his whole heart?

sentences.zh: 臣欲正衙彈劾，不敢不先聞奏。」

translations.literal: I wish to impeach him at formal court but dare not fail to report first."
translations.idiomatic: I mean to impeach him at court but dared report to you first."

sentences.zh: 上由是惡琯，詔以進明為河南節度、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore came to dislike Guan and ordered Jinming made Henan commissioner and also Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned against Guan and made Jinming Henan commissioner and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 崔圓本蜀中拜相，肅宗幸扶風，始來朝謁。

translations.literal: Cui Yuan had originally been made chancellor in Shu; when Suzong reached Fufeng he first came to audience.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuan had been made chancellor in Shu; when Suzong reached Fufeng, Yuan first presented himself.

sentences.zh: 琯意以為圓才到，當即免相，故待圓禮薄。

translations.literal: Guan thought Yuan had only just arrived and would at once be removed from the chancellery, so he treated Yuan with thin courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Guan assumed Yuan would soon be dismissed and treated him coldly.

sentences.zh: 圓厚結李輔國，到後數日，頗承恩渥，亦憾於琯。

translations.literal: Yuan cultivated Li Fuguo closely; within days he enjoyed great favor and also resented Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan courted Li Fuguo, won favor within days, and resented Guan in turn.

sentences.zh: 琯又多稱病，不時朝謁，於政事簡惰。

translations.literal: Guan also often claimed illness and did not attend court on schedule, and was slack in government.
translations.idiomatic: Guan often pleaded illness, skipped court, and neglected affairs.

sentences.zh: 時議以兩京陷賊，車駕出次外郊，天下人心惴恐。

translations.literal: Public opinion held that with both capitals fallen and the imperial carriage encamped outside, the hearts of the empire were fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Both capitals had fallen and the court was in the field; the realm was afraid.

sentences.zh: 當主憂臣辱之際，此時琯為宰相，略無匪懈之意，但與庶子劉秩、諫議李揖、何忌等高談虛論，說釋氏因果、老子虛無而已。

translations.literal: At a time when the ruler should grieve and ministers feel shame, Guan as chancellor showed hardly any tireless effort but only held high talk with Liu Zhi, Li Yi, He Ji, and others on Buddhist karma and Laozi's emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler should mourn and ministers blush, Guan as chancellor showed no diligence—only talked karma and Laozi with Liu Zhi, Li Yi, and He Ji.

sentences.zh: 此外，則聽董庭蘭彈琴，大招集琴客筵宴。

translations.literal: Otherwise he listened to Dong Tinglan play the qin and gave great banquets gathering qin players.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise he listened to Dong Tinglan on the qin and held banquets for musicians.

sentences.zh: 朝官往往因庭蘭以見琯，自是亦大招納貨賄，奸贓頗甚。

translations.literal: Court officials often reached Guan through Tinglan, and from then on he also took large bribes; corruption was considerable.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reached him through Tinglan, and he took heavy bribes.

sentences.zh: 顏真卿時為大夫，彈何忌不孝，琯既黨何忌，遽托以酒醉入朝，貶為西平郡司馬。

translations.literal: Yan Zhenqing was then senior censor and impeached He Ji for unfilial conduct; Guan, siding with He Ji, pretended drunkenness at court and had Zhenqing demoted to Sima of Xiping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing impeached He Ji for unfilial conduct; Guan protected He Ji, feigned drunkenness at court, and had Zhenqing demoted.

sentences.zh: 憲司又奏彈董庭蘭招納貨賄，琯入朝自訴，上叱出之，因歸私第，不敢預人事。

translations.literal: The censorate also impeached Dong Tinglan for taking bribes; Guan came to court to plead and the emperor shouted him out; he returned home and dared not meddle in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate impeached Tinglan for bribes; Guan pleaded at court, was shouted away, went home, and dared not meddle.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫張鎬上疏，言琯大臣，門客受贓，不宜見累。

translations.literal: Remonstrating censor Zhang Gao memorialized that Guan was a great minister and that retainers taking bribes should not stain him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Gao said a great minister should not be stained by retainers' bribes.

sentences.zh: 二年五月，貶為太子少師，仍以鎬代琯為宰相。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year he was demoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Gao replaced Guan as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 2 he was demoted to Junior Mentor; Gao replaced him.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，從肅宗還京師。

translations.literal: That eleventh month he followed Suzong back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That eleventh month he followed Suzong to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 十二月，大赦，策勛行賞，加琯金紫光祿大夫，進封清河郡公。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, at the great amnesty and reward for merit, Guan was given the gold and purple glory grandee rank and advanced to Duke of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: At the twelfth-month amnesty he received Gold and Purple Glory Grandee rank and was made Duke of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 琯既在散位，朝臣多以為言，琯亦常自言有文武之用，合當國家驅策，冀蒙任遇。

translations.literal: Though Guan held no active post, many courtiers spoke for him; Guan too often said he had civil and military use and ought to drive the state, hoping for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Out of office, courtiers still spoke for him; he claimed civil and military gifts and hoped to be used.

sentences.zh: 又招納賓客，朝夕盈門，遊其門者，又將琯言議暴揚於朝。

translations.literal: He again gathered guests until his doors were full morning and evening, and those who visited spread Guan's talk in court.
translations.idiomatic: He again filled his house with guests, and visitors spread his opinions at court.

sentences.zh: 琯又多稱疾，上頗不悅。

translations.literal: Guan also often claimed illness, and the emperor grew displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He often pleaded illness, and the emperor grew annoyed.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年六月，詔曰：

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Qianyuan an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan 1, sixth month, an edict declared:

sentences.zh: 崇黨近名，實為害政之本；

translations.literal: Favoring cliques and chasing reputation is truly the root of harm to government;
translations.idiomatic: Favoring cliques and chasing fame harms government at the root;

sentences.zh: 黜華去薄，方啟至公之路。

translations.literal: removing display and rejecting shallowness opens the road to utmost fairness.
translations.idiomatic: casting off display opens the road to true fairness.

sentences.zh: 房琯素表文學，夙推名器，由是累階清貴，致位臺衡。

translations.literal: Fang Guan has long shown literary talent and been pushed as a famous vessel; by this he rose through pure offices to the pinnacle.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guan rose on literary fame to the highest offices.

sentences.zh: 而率情自任，怙氣恃權。

translations.literal: Yet he indulged his feelings and relied on arrogant power.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he indulged feeling and arrogant power.

sentences.zh: 虛浮簡傲者進為同人，溫讓謹令者捐於異路。

translations.literal: The frivolous and proud advanced as his kind; the warm and careful were cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: The frivolous advanced; the careful were pushed aside.

sentences.zh: 所以輔佐之際，謀猷匪弘。

translations.literal: Therefore in assisting rule his plans were not broad.
translations.idiomatic: In counsel his plans were never broad.

sentences.zh: 頃者時屬艱難，擢居將相，朕永懷反席，冀有成功。

translations.literal: Lately in hardship he was raised to general and chancellor; I ever hoped he would succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Raised in crisis, I hoped he would succeed.

sentences.zh: 而喪我師徒，既虧制勝之任；

translations.literal: Yet he lost my armies and failed the charge of victory;
translations.idiomatic: He lost armies and failed to win;

sentences.zh: 升其親友，悉彰浮誕之跡。

translations.literal: promoted his kin and friends, fully showing frivolous traces.
translations.idiomatic: he promoted kin and friends in frivolous fashion.

sentences.zh: 曾未逾時，遽從敗績。

translations.literal: Before long he met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was beaten.

sentences.zh: 自合首明軍令，以謝師旅，猶尚矜其萬死，擢以三孤。

translations.literal: By military law he should have answered with his head, yet I still0 spared his life and raised him among the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: By law he should have died; I spared him and made him one of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 或云緣其切直，遂見斥退。

translations.literal: Some say because he was blunt and straight he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Some say blunt honesty caused his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 朕示以堂案，令觀所以，鹹知乖舛，曠於政事。

translations.literal: I showed him the records so he would see how he had erred and neglected government.
translations.idiomatic: I showed him records of his errors in government.

sentences.zh: 誠宜效茲忠懇，以奉國家，而乃多稱疾疹，莫申朝謁。

translations.literal: He ought to show loyal earnestness for the state, yet he often claims illness and does not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: He should serve loyally, yet claims illness and skips court.

sentences.zh: 郤犨為政，曾不疾其迂回；

translations.literal: Xi Que in government did not fault his roundabout ways;
translations.idiomatic: Xi Que did not fault roundabout ways;

sentences.zh: 亞夫事君，翻有懷於郁怏。

translations.literal: Zhou Yafu serving his lord yet harbored gloom.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yafu harbored gloom serving his lord.

sentences.zh: 又與前國子祭酒劉秩、前京兆少尹嚴武等潛為交結，輕肆言談，有朋黨不公之名，違臣子奉上之體。

translations.literal: He also secretly joined with former Guozi Academy director Liu Zhi and former metropolitan vice governor Yan Wu in reckless talk, gaining a name for faction and violating a subject's duty to serve above.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly joined Liu Zhi and Yan Wu in reckless talk, factional and disloyal.

sentences.zh: 何以儀刑王國，訓導儲闈？

translations.literal: How can he model the royal domain and instruct the heir?
translations.idiomatic: How can he model the realm or instruct the heir?

sentences.zh: 但以嘗踐臺司，未忍致之於理。

translations.literal: Only because he once stood at the Secretariat I have not sent him to law.
translations.idiomatic: Because he once held high office I have not prosecuted him.

sentences.zh: 況秩、武遽更相尚，同務虛求，不議典章，何成沮勸？

translations.literal: Moreover Zhi and Wu now flatter each other in empty pursuit, not discussing statutes—what discouragement is that?
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and Wu flatter each other in emptiness—what example is that?

sentences.zh: 宜從貶秩，俾守外籓。

translations.literal: They should be demoted to guard outer prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: They should be demoted to outer prefectures.

sentences.zh: 琯可邠州刺史，秩可閬州刺史，武可巴州刺史，散官、封如故；

translations.literal: Guan may be made prefect of Bin, Zhi of Lang, Wu of Ba; honorary ranks and fiefs unchanged;
translations.idiomatic: Guan to Binzhou, Zhi to Langzhou, Wu to Bazhou; ranks unchanged;

sentences.zh: 並即馳驛赴任，庶各增修。

translations.literal: and each is to hurry by post to his post so they may reform.
translations.idiomatic: each is to hurry by post to his post and reform.

sentences.zh: 朕自臨禦寰區，薦延多士，常思聿求賢哲，共致雍熙。

translations.literal: Since I took the realm I have promoted many men, ever seeking worthy men to bring peace.
translations.idiomatic: Since I took the throne I have sought worthy men for peace.

sentences.zh: 深嫉比周之徒，虛偽成俗。

translations.literal: I deeply hate faction-makers and the habit of falsity.
translations.idiomatic: I hate factions and falsity.

sentences.zh: 今茲所譴，實屬其辜。

translations.literal: Today's punishments truly fit their guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Today's punishments fit their guilt.

sentences.zh: 猶以琯等妄自標持，假延浮稱，雖周行具悉，恐流俗多疑，所以事必縷言，蓋欲人知不濫。

translations.literal: Still, because Guan and the rest falsely advertise themselves and borrow floating praise, though the court knows all, I fear the vulgar will doubt, and so I speak in detail lest people think it arbitrary.
translations.idiomatic: Though the court knows them, I speak in detail lest the crowd think me arbitrary.

sentences.zh: 凡百卿士，宜悉朕懷。

translations.literal: All you ministers should understand my heart.
translations.idiomatic: All ministers should understand my intent.

sentences.zh: 時邠州久屯軍旅，多以武將兼領刺史，法度隳廢，州縣廨宇，並為軍營，官吏侵奪百姓室屋以居，人甚弊之。

translations.literal: At that time Binzhou had long quartered armies; military men often concurrently held the prefecture, laws and regulations collapsed, prefectural and county government buildings all became military camps, and officials seized commoners' houses to live in, to the people's great distress.
translations.idiomatic: Binzhou had long housed troops; generals often doubled as prefect, discipline collapsed, government buildings became barracks, and officials seized civilians' homes—greatly harming the people.

sentences.zh: 琯到任，舉陳令式，令州縣恭守，又緝理公館，僚吏各歸官曹，頗著政聲。

translations.literal: When Guan took office he cited Chen Ling-shi's regulations, ordered prefectures and counties to observe them respectfully, also put the public offices in order, and had staff return to their proper bureaus, winning a considerable reputation for good government.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Guan cited Chen Ling-shi's regulations, required prefectures and counties to observe them, restored the public offices, and sent staff back to their proper posts, winning a good reputation.

sentences.zh: 二年六月，詔褒美之，征拜太子賓客。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year an edict praised him and he was summoned as Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year an edict praised him and he was summoned as Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 上元元年四月，改禮部尚書，尋出為晉州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Shangyuan he was changed to Minister of Rites and soon sent out as prefect of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Shangyuan 1 he became Minister of Rites and soon went out as Jinzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 八月，改漢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was changed to prefect of Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he became Hanzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 琯長子乘，自少兩目盲。

translations.literal: Guan's eldest son Cheng had been blind in both eyes since childhood.
translations.idiomatic: Guan's eldest son Cheng had been blind since childhood.

sentences.zh: 琯到漢州，乃厚結司馬李銳以財貨，乘聘銳外甥女盧氏，時議薄其無士行。

translations.literal: When Guan reached Hanzhou he lavishly cultivated Vice-Prefect Li Rui with goods and wealth, and Cheng married Rui's niece of the Lu clan; public opinion looked down on his lack of gentlemanly conduct.
translations.idiomatic: At Hanzhou Guan lavishly cultivated Vice-Prefect Li Rui with gifts so Cheng could marry Rui's niece, surnamed Lu; opinion condemned his want of proper conduct.

sentences.zh: 寶應二年四月，拜特進、刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Baoying he was appointed Special Advancement and Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Baoying 2 he was made Special Advancement and Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 在路遇疾，廣德元年八月四日，卒於閬州僧舍，時年六十七。

translations.literal: On the road he fell ill; on the fourth day of the eighth month of the first year of Guangde he died in a Langzhou monastery at the age of sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill on the road and died in a Langzhou monastery on the fourth day of the eighth month of Guangde 1, aged sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 孺復，琯之孽子也。

translations.literal: Rufu was Guan's illegitimate son.
translations.idiomatic: Rufu was Guan's bastard son.

sentences.zh: 少黠慧，年七八歲，即粗解綴文，親黨奇之。

translations.literal: As a child he was clever; at seven or eight he could already string words, and kin marveled.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was clever; at seven or eight he could compose, and kin marveled.

sentences.zh: 稍長，狂疏傲慢，任情縱欲。

translations.literal: Growing older he was wild, rude, and arrogant and indulged his desires.
translations.idiomatic: Older, he was wild, rude, and self-indulgent.

sentences.zh: 年二十，淮南節度陳少遊辟為從事，多招陰陽巫覡，令揚言已過三十必為宰相。

translations.literal: At twenty Huainan Commissioner Chen Shaoyou made him an aide; he gathered many yin-yang shamans to proclaim he would surely be chancellor after thirty.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty Chen Shaoyou made him an aide; shamans said he would be chancellor after thirty.

sentences.zh: 德宗幸奉天，包佶掌賦於揚州，少遊將抑奪之。

translations.literal: When Dezong reached Fengtian, Bao Ji was managing taxes at Yangzhou and Shaoyou was about to seize them.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong reached Fengtian, Bao Ji managed Yangzhou taxes and Shaoyou meant to seize them.

sentences.zh: 佶聞而奔出，少遊方遣人劫佶令回，孺復請行，會佶已過江南，乃還。

translations.literal: Ji heard and fled; Shaoyou was about to send men to force Ji back when Rufu asked to go, but Ji had already passed south of the river and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ji fled; Shaoyou sent men to force him back; Rufu volunteered, but Ji was already south of the river.

sentences.zh: 及少遊卒，浙西節度韓滉又辟入幕。

translations.literal: After Shaoyou died, Zhexi Commissioner Han Huang again took him on staff.
translations.idiomatic: After Shaoyou died, Han Huang of Zhexi took him on staff.

sentences.zh: 其長兄宗偃先貶官嶺下而卒，及喪柩到揚州，孺復未嘗吊。

translations.literal: His elder brother Zongyan had earlier been demoted to the south and died; when the coffin reached Yangzhou Rufu never mourned.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Zongyan had died in exile; when the coffin reached Yangzhou Rufu did not mourn.

sentences.zh: 初娶鄭氏，惡賤其妻，多畜婢仆，妻之保母累言之，孺復乃先具棺櫬而集家人，生斂保母，遠近驚異。

translations.literal: He first married the Zheng clan and despised his wife, keeping many maids; the wife's nurse spoke repeatedly and Rufu prepared coffins, gathered kin, and buried the nurse alive—near and far were shocked.
translations.idiomatic: He married a Zheng, despised her, kept maids; when her nurse complained he buried the nurse alive—shocking all.

sentences.zh: 及妻在產蓐三四日，遽令上船即路，數日，妻遇風而卒。

translations.literal: When his wife was in childbirth three or four days he suddenly ordered her aboard ship and on the road; within days she died in a storm.
translations.idiomatic: While his wife lay in childbirth he put her on a ship; days later she died in a storm.

sentences.zh: 孺復以宰相子，年少有浮名，而奸惡未甚露，累拜杭州刺史。

translations.literal: Rufu, as a chancellor's son with a floating name though his wickedness was not fully exposed, was repeatedly made prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As a chancellor's son with a name, though wickedness was hidden, he became Hangzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 又娶臺州刺史崔昭女，崔妒悍甚，一夕杖殺孺復待兒二人，埋之雪中。

translations.literal: He again married the daughter of Prefect Cui Zhao of Taizhou; Cui was fiercely jealous and one night beat two of Rufu's attendants to death and buried them in snow.
translations.idiomatic: He married Cui Zhao's daughter; she beat two attendants to death and buried them in snow.

sentences.zh: 觀察使聞之，詔發使鞫案有實，孺復坐貶連州司馬，仍令與崔氏離異。

translations.literal: The observation commissioner heard, ordered investigation, found truth, Rufu was demoted to Sima of Lianzhou and ordered separated from Cui.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation proved it; he was demoted to Lianzhou Sima and divorced.

sentences.zh: 孺復久之遷辰州刺史，改容州刺史、本管經略使。

translations.literal: After long service he was moved to Chenzhou prefect and Rongzhou prefect and military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Chenzhou prefect, then Rongzhou prefect and commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乃潛與妻往來，久而上疏請合，詔從之。

translations.literal: He secretly met his wife again; after long time he memorialized to reunite and an edict allowed it.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly reunited with his wife and later won permission to remarry.

sentences.zh: 二歲餘，又奏與崔氏離異，其為取舍恣逸，不顧禮法也如此。

translations.literal: After more than two years he again memorialized to separate from Cui—so capricious and heedless of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he divorced her again—heedless of ritual.

sentences.zh: 貞元十三年九月卒，時年四十二。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the thirteenth year of Zhenyuan he died at forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 13, ninth month, he died at forty-two.

sentences.zh: 式，琯之姪，舉進士。

translations.literal: Shi was Guan's nephew and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was Guan's nephew and a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 李泌觀察陜州，辟為從事。

translations.literal: Li Bi, observing Shaanzhou, made him an aide.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi at Shaanzhou made him an aide.

sentences.zh: 泌入為相，累遷起居郎，出入泌門，為其耳目。

translations.literal: When Bi entered the chancellery Shi rose to Attendant and went in and out of Bi's house as his eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: When Bi became chancellor Shi became Attendant and served as his eyes and ears.

sentences.zh: 及泌卒，再除忠州刺史，韋臯表為雲南安撫使，兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: After Bi died he was twice made prefect of Zhongzhou; Wei Gao recommended him as Yunnan pacification commissioner and also Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After Bi's death he was Zhongzhou prefect; Wei Gao made him Yunnan pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 臯卒，詔除兵部郎中。

translations.literal: When Gao died an edict made him director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao died he was made director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 屬劉辟反，式留不得行。

translations.literal: Liu Pi rebelled and Shi could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi rebelled and Shi could not leave.

sentences.zh: 性便佞，又懼辟，每於座中數贊辟之德美，比之劉備，同陷於賊者皆惡之。

translations.literal: By nature he was fawning; fearing Pi, at meetings he often praised Pi as virtuous, comparing him to Liu Bei—all trapped with the rebels hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Fawning and afraid of Pi, he praised Pi like Liu Bei—hated by loyalists.

sentences.zh: 高崇文既至成都，式與王良士、崔從、盧士玖等白衣麻蹻銜土請罪，崇文寬禮之，乃表其狀，尋除吏部郎中。

translations.literal: When Gao Chongwen reached Chengdu, Shi with Wang Liangshi, Cui Cong, Lu Shiqiu, and others in white hemp and carrying soil begged pardon; Chongwen treated them generously, reported their case, and soon Shi was made director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwen pardoned Shi and soon made him Personnel director.

sentences.zh: 時河朔節度劉濟、王士真、張茂昭皆以兵壯氣豪，相持短長，屢以表聞，叠請加罪。

translations.literal: At that time Hebei commissioners Liu Ji, Wang Shizhen, and Zhang Maozhao were all strong and proud and often sent conflicting memorials asking for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei commissioners Liu Ji, Wang Shizhen, and Zhang Maozhao were strong and quarrelsome.

sentences.zh: 上欲止其兵，李吉甫薦式為給事中，將命於河朔。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to stop their armies; Li Jifu recommended Shi as supervising secretary to send to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted peace; Li Jifu recommended Shi as envoy.

sentences.zh: 式歷使諸鎮諷諭之，還奏愜旨，除陜虢觀察使、兼御史中丞，轉河南尹。

translations.literal: Shi toured the circuits persuading them; on return his report pleased the throne and he was made Shaan-Guo observation commissioner and also Vice Censor-in-Chief, then Henan metropolitan governor.
translations.idiomatic: His mission pleased the throne; he became Shaan-Guo commissioner, then Henan governor.

sentences.zh: 時討王丞宗於鎮州，配河南府饋運車四千兩，式表以兇旱，人貧力微，難以征發，憲宗可其奏，既免力役，人懷而安之。

translations.literal: When Wang Chengzong was attacked at Zhenzhou, four thousand Henan supply carts were assigned; Shi memorialized that famine made levies impossible and Xianzong approved, sparing labor so the people were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenzhou campaign he won relief from impossible levies.

sentences.zh: 明年，移授宣歙池觀察使。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Xu-Xuan-Chi observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he became Xu-Xuan-Chi commissioner.

sentences.zh: 元和七年七月卒，贈左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the seventh year of Yuanhe he died and was posthumously made Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 7, seventh month, he died; posthumously Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 張鎬，博州人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Gao was a man of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gao was from Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 風儀魁岸，廓落有大志，涉獵經史，好談王霸大略。

translations.literal: His bearing was imposing and he had great ambitions; he read classics and histories and loved discussing hegemonic strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Imposing in bearing, ambitious, learned, fond of grand strategy.

sentences.zh: 少時師事吳兢，兢甚重之。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Wu Jing, whom Jing greatly valued.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under Wu Jing, who valued him.

sentences.zh: 後遊京師，端居一室，不交世務。

translations.literal: Later in the capital he lived alone in one room and did not mix in worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he lived alone and shunned worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 性嗜酒，好琴，常置座右。

translations.literal: He loved wine and the qin and always kept them at his right hand.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and the qin and kept them at hand.

sentences.zh: 公卿或有邀之者，鎬仗策徑往，求醉而已。

translations.literal: When grandees invited him Gao would go staff in hand seeking only to get drunk.
translations.idiomatic: When invited he went staff in hand seeking only drink.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，楊國忠以聲名自高，搜天下奇傑。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao Yang Guozhong, proud of his fame, searched the empire for extraordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tianbao Yang Guozhong sought extraordinary men.

sentences.zh: 聞鎬名，召見薦之，自褐衣拜左拾遺。

translations.literal: Hearing Gao's name he summoned and recommended him; from commoner he was made Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Gao's name he summoned him—from commoner to Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 及祿山阻兵，國忠屢以軍國事咨於鎬，鎬舉贊善大夫來瑱可當方面之寄。

translations.literal: When Lushan blocked the roads Guozhong often consulted Gao on military affairs; Gao recommended Zan Shan Grandee Lai Tian as fit to hold a frontier post.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled Guozhong consulted Gao, who recommended Lai Tian for frontier command.

sentences.zh: 數月，玄宗幸蜀，鎬自山谷徒步扈從。

translations.literal: Months later Xuanzong fled to Shu and Gao followed on foot from the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong fled to Shu Gao followed on foot.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，玄宗遣鎬赴行在所。

translations.literal: When Suzong took the throne Xuanzong sent Gao to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong's accession sent Gao to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 鎬至鳳翔，奏識多有弘益，拜諫議大夫，尋遷中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Reaching Fengxiang his memorials were often beneficial and he was made remonstrating censor, soon Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengxiang his advice helped; he became remonstrating censor, then vice director and councillor.

sentences.zh: 時供奉僧在內道場晨夜念佛，動數百人，聲聞禁外。

translations.literal: At that time offering monks in the inner chapel chanted day and night, several hundred at a time, their voices heard outside the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Monks in the inner chapel chanted day and night by the hundreds, heard outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 鎬奏曰：「臣聞天子修福，要在安養含生，靖一風化，未聞區區僧教，以致太平。

translations.literal: Gao memorialized, "I have heard that when the Son of Heaven cultivates blessing, the point is to nurture all living beings and settle custom; I have not heard that petty Buddhist teaching brings great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Gao wrote, "A ruler's blessing lies in nurturing life and settling custom—not in petty Buddhist teaching for peace.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下以無為為心，不以小乘而撓聖慮。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to take non-action as your heart and not let small vehicles disturb the sage's thought."
translations.idiomatic: Take non-action as your heart and do not let small teachings disturb your mind."

sentences.zh: 肅宗甚然之。

translations.literal: Suzong greatly approved.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 時方興軍戎，帝註意將帥，以鎬有文武才，尋命兼河南節度使，持節都統淮南等道諸軍事。

translations.literal: At that time armies were being raised; the emperor focused on generals and, because Gao had civil and military talent, soon also ordered him Henan military commissioner with full powers over Huainan and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: With war rising, the emperor noted Gao's civil and military gifts and made him Henan commissioner with powers over Huainan.

sentences.zh: 鎬既發，會張巡宋州圍急，倍道兼進，傳檄濠州刺史閭丘曉引兵出救。

translations.literal: After Gao set out, Songzhou under Zhang Xun was in desperate siege; he marched day and night and sent a proclamation to Chuzhou Prefect Yan Qiu Xiao to lead troops to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Marching out, he learned Songzhou under Zhang Xun was besieged; he rushed and ordered Chuzhou's Yan Qiu Xiao to rescue.

sentences.zh: 曉素愎戾，馭下少恩，好獨任己。

translations.literal: Xiao was by nature obstinate, showed little kindness to subordinates, and liked to act alone.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao was obstinate, unkind to subordinates, and self-willed.

sentences.zh: 及鎬信至，略無稟命，又慮兵敗，禍及於己，遂逗留不進。

translations.literal: When Gao's letter arrived he barely obeyed orders, also fearing defeat would harm him, and so lingered without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: He barely obeyed, feared defeat would ruin him, and lingered.

sentences.zh: 鎬至淮口，宋州已陷，鎬怒曉，即杖殺之。

translations.literal: Gao reached the Huai mouth; Songzhou had already fallen and Gao in anger executed Xiao on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: At the Huai mouth Songzhou had fallen; Gao angrily had Xiao beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 及收復兩京，加鎬銀青光祿大夫，封南陽郡公，詔以本軍鎮汴州，招討殘孽。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were recovered Gao was given silver and blue glory grandee rank and enfeoffed Duke of Nanyang; an edict had his army garrison Bianzhou to mop up remnants.
translations.idiomatic: After recovering the capitals he was made Silver and Blue Glory Grandee and Duke of Nanyang, garrisoning Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 時賊帥史思明表請以范陽歸順，鎬揣知其偽，恐朝廷許之，手書密表奏曰：「思明兇豎，因逆竊位，兵強則眾附，勢奪則人離。

translations.literal: At that time rebel leader Shi Siming petitioned to submit from Fanyang; Gao guessed the falseness and feared the court would accept, and in a secret hand memorial said, "Siming is a vicious fellow who stole rank by rebellion; when his army is strong the masses follow, when power slips men leave.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming offered submission from Fanyang; Gao saw the fraud and secretly warned, "Siming is a rebel beast—strong when followed, deserted when weak.

sentences.zh: 包藏不測，禽獸無異，可以計取，難以義招。

translations.literal: He harbors the unknowable, no different from beasts; he can be taken by stratagem, hard to win by righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He is unknowable as a beast; take him by stratagem, not by righteousness.

sentences.zh: 伏望不以威權假之。」

translations.literal: I beg that authority not be lent to his prestige."
translations.idiomatic: Do not lend him your authority."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「滑州防禦使許叔冀，性狡多謀，臨難必變，望追入宿衛。」

translations.literal: He also said, "Huazhou defense commissioner Xu Shuji is crafty and full of schemes and will surely change in crisis; I beg he be recalled to palace guard."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Xu Shuji, defense commissioner of Huazhou, is crafty and full of schemes and will surely turn in crisis; I beg he be recalled to palace guard."

sentences.zh: 肅宗計意已定，表入不省。

translations.literal: Suzong's plan was already set and the memorials were not examined.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong's mind was set; the memorials were ignored.

sentences.zh: 鎬為人簡淡，不事中要。

translations.literal: Gao was by nature simple and indifferent and did not court powerful favorites.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was simple and did not court favorites.

sentences.zh: 會有宦官自范陽及滑州使還者，皆言思明、叔冀之誠愨。

translations.literal: Eunuchs returning from Fanyang and Huazhou all said Siming and Shuji were sincere.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs from Fanyang and Huazhou said Siming and Shuji were sincere.

sentences.zh: 肅宗以鎬不切事機，遂罷相位，授荊州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: Suzong thought Gao did not grasp affairs and removed him from the chancellery, making him chief of Jingzhou metropolitan government.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong thought Gao inept and made him Jingzhou chief.

sentences.zh: 後思明、叔冀之偽皆符鎬言。

translations.literal: Later Siming's and Shuji's falseness both matched Gao's words.
translations.idiomatic: Later both proved Gao right.

sentences.zh: 尋征為太子賓客，改左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Mentor of the Heir Apparent and changed to Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was later Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 屬嗣岐王珍被誣告構逆伏法，鎬買珍宅坐累，貶辰州司戶。

translations.literal: When the heir Prince Zhen was falsely accused of plotting treason and executed, Gao bought Zhen's house and was implicated, demoted to Sima of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhen was executed for treason, Gao bought his house and was demoted to Chenzhou Sima.

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，推恩海內，拜撫州刺史。

translations.literal: When Daizong took the throne he extended grace across the sea and made Gao prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong's grace made him Fuzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 遷洪州刺史、饒吉等七州都團練觀察等使，尋正授江南西道都團練觀察等使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hongzhou prefect and observation commissioner of Rao, Ji, and seven other prefectures, soon regular Jiangnan West Circuit observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He became Hongzhou prefect and Jiangnan West commissioner.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年九月卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Guangde he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangde 2, ninth month, he died.

sentences.zh: 鎬自入仕凡三年，致位宰相。

translations.literal: From entering office Gao held the chancellery only three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: In only three years of service he reached the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 居身清廉，不營資產，謙恭下士，善談論，多識大體，故天下具瞻，雖考秩至淺，推為舊德云。

translations.literal: He lived in integrity without amassing property, was humble to inferiors, loved discussion, knew great principles, and so the empire looked up to him; though his examination rank was shallow he was honored as an elder.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, without wealth, humble and wise, he was honored as an elder though his rank was low.

sentences.zh: 高適者，渤海蓚人也。

translations.literal: Gao Shi was a man of Boling Tiao.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shi was from Boling Tiao.

sentences.zh: 父從文，位終韶州長史。

translations.literal: His father Congwen ended as chief of Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Congwen died as chief of Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 適少濩落，不事生業，家貧，客於梁、宋，以求丐取給。

translations.literal: Shi in youth was unsettled and did not pursue a livelihood; the family was poor and he sojourned in Liang and Song seeking support.
translations.idiomatic: Young Shi was unsettled and poor, living by favor in Liang and Song.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，海內事幹進者註意文詞。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era those seeking advancement in the realm focused on literary skill.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao men sought office through letters.

sentences.zh: 適年過五十，始留意詩什，數年之間，體格漸變，以氣質自高，每吟一篇，已為好事者稱誦。

translations.literal: Past fifty Shi first turned to poetry; within years his style changed and, confident in his temperament, each poem he recited was praised by enthusiasts.
translations.idiomatic: Past fifty he took up poetry; soon each poem won praise.

sentences.zh: 宋州刺史張九臯深奇之，薦舉有道科。

translations.literal: Songzhou Prefect Zhang Jiugao greatly admired him and recommended him for the dao examination.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhou's Zhang Jiugao recommended him for the dao examination.

sentences.zh: 時右相李林甫擅權，薄於文雅，唯以舉子待之。

translations.literal: Right Chancellor Li Linfu monopolized power and slighted letters, treating candidates only as examination entrants.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu slighted letters and treated candidates coldly.

sentences.zh: 解褐汴州封丘尉，非其好也，乃去位，客遊河右。

translations.literal: Released from office as Wei of Fengqiu in Bianzhou—it was not to his taste—and he left to wander west of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Made Wei of Fengqiu, he disliked it and wandered west.

sentences.zh: 河西節度哥舒翰見而異之。

translations.literal: Hexi Commissioner Ge Shu Han was struck by him.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Shu Han of Hexi was struck by him.

sentences.zh: 表為左驍衛兵曹，充翰府掌書記，從翰入朝，盛稱之於上前。

translations.literal: He was memorialized as Left Valiant Guard records officer and secretary in Han's headquarters; following Han to court he was greatly praised before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Han made him secretary and praised him at court.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，征翰討賊，拜適左拾遺，轉監察御史，仍佐翰守潼關。

translations.literal: In Lushan's rebellion Han was sent to suppress the rebels; Shi was made Left Reminder, then investigating censor, still assisting Han at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the rebellion he became Left Reminder and censor, aiding Han at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 及翰兵敗，適自駱谷西馳，奔赴行在，及河池郡，謁見玄宗，因陳潼關敗亡之勢曰：「僕射哥舒翰忠義感激，臣頗知之，然疾病沈頓，智力將竭。

translations.literal: When Han was defeated Shi galloped west through Lu Valley to the mobile court; at Hechi Commandery he presented himself to Xuanzong and described Tong Pass's fall: "Vice Marshal Ge Shu Han is loyal and grateful—I know him well—but illness weighed him down and his wit was failing.
translations.idiomatic: When Han fell he raced to the mobile court and told Xuanzong, "Vice Marshal Ge Shu Han is loyal and grateful—I know him well—but illness weighed him down and his wit was failing.

sentences.zh: 監軍李大宜與將士約為香火，使倡婦彈箜篌琵琶以相娛樂，樗蒱飲酒，不恤軍務。

translations.literal: Supervisor Li Dayi made incense vows with the troops and had singing women play pipa and zither for amusement, gambling and drinking, heedless of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor Li Dayi had troops gamble and drink with singing women, heedless of war.

sentences.zh: 蕃渾及秦、隴武士，盛夏五六月於赤日之中，食倉米飯且猶不足，欲其勇戰，安可得乎？

translations.literal: Tangut and Qin-Long warriors in the fifth and sixth months of summer ate warehouse rice and were still not full—how could they fight bravely?
translations.idiomatic: Tangut and Qin-Long soldiers in summer heat lacked even rice—how fight bravely?

sentences.zh: 故有望敵散亡，臨陣翻動，萬全之地，一朝而失。

translations.literal: Therefore they looked at the enemy and scattered, wavered in battle, and in a place that should have been secure lost all in a morning.
translations.idiomatic: So they broke before the enemy and lost a secure pass in a morning.

sentences.zh: 南陽之軍，魯炅、何履光、趙國珍各皆持節，監軍等數人更相用事，寧有是，戰而能必勝哉？

translations.literal: The Nanyang army—Lu Ling, He Lüguang, Zhao Guozhen—each held full powers and several supervisors quarreled; could such men surely win?
translations.idiomatic: Nanyang commanders each held seals and quarreled—could they win?

sentences.zh: 臣與楊國忠爭，終不見納。

translations.literal: I contended with Yang Guozhong and was never heeded.
translations.idiomatic: I argued with Yang Guozhong in vain.

sentences.zh: 陛下因此履巴山、劍閣之險，西幸蜀中，避其蠆毒，未足為恥也。」
