translations.literal: Your Majesty therefore walked the dangers of Ba Mountain and Sword Pass to Shu to avoid poison—no shame in that."
translations.idiomatic: You fled to Shu to avoid poison—no shame in that."

sentences.zh: 玄宗嘉之，尋遷侍御史。

translations.literal: Xuanzong praised him and soon made him attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong praised him and made him attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 至成都，八月，制曰：「侍御史高適，立節貞峻，植躬高朗，感激懷經濟之略，紛綸贍文雅之才。

translations.literal: At Chengdu in the eighth month an edict said, "Attendant censor Gao Shi stands upright and bright, cherishes economy, stirred by strategy, rich in letters.
translations.idiomatic: At Chengdu an edict said, "Attendant censor Gao Shi stands upright and bright, stirred by strategy, rich in letters.

sentences.zh: 長策遠圖，可雲大體；

translations.literal: Long plans and far sight can be called great principle;
translations.idiomatic: Long plans are great principle;

sentences.zh: 讜言義色，實謂忠臣。

translations.literal: loyal words and righteous color truly make a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: loyal words make a loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 宜回糾逖之任，俾超諷諭之職，可諫議大夫，賜緋魚袋。」

translations.literal: He should return from distant censure to surpass remonstrance; he may be remonstrating grandee with crimson fish bag."
translations.idiomatic: Make him remonstrating grandee with crimson fish."

sentences.zh: 適負氣敢言，權幸憚之。

translations.literal: Shi was bold in speech and the powerful feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi spoke boldly and the powerful feared him.

sentences.zh: 二年，永王璘起兵於江東，欲據揚州。

translations.literal: In the second year Prince Yong of Jiangdong raised troops intending to hold Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 Prince Yong raised troops for Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，上皇以諸王分鎮，適切諫不可。

translations.literal: Earlier the Retired Emperor had the princes divide command; Shi had urgently remonstrated that it should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shi had warned against dividing the princes' commands.

sentences.zh: 及是永王叛，肅宗聞其論諫有素，召而謀之。

translations.literal: Now Prince Yong rebelled; Suzong, hearing his long-standing advice, summoned him to counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong rebelled, Suzong recalled Shi's earlier advice.

sentences.zh: 適因陳江東利害，永王必敗。

translations.literal: Shi explained the advantages and dangers of Jiangdong; Yong would surely fail.
translations.idiomatic: Shi explained Jiangdong; Yong would fail.

sentences.zh: 上奇其對，以適兼御史大夫、揚州大都督府長史、淮南節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at the answer and made Shi also Censor-in-Chief, chief of Yangzhou metropolitan government, and Huainan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made him Censor-in-Chief, Yangzhou chief, and Huainan commissioner.

sentences.zh: 詔與江東節度來瑱率本部兵平江淮之亂，會於安州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him with Jiangdong Commissioner Lai Tian to lead their troops to pacify Jiang-Huai disorder, meeting at Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He and Lai Tian were to pacify Jiang-Huai at Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 師將渡而永王敗，乃招季廣琛於歷陽。

translations.literal: The army was about to cross when Yong was defeated; he then summoned Ji Guangchen at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before crossing, Yong fell; he summoned Ji Guangchen at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 兵罷，李輔國惡適敢言，短於上前，乃左授太子少詹事。

translations.literal: When the army was dismissed Li Fuguo hated Shi's bold speech and slandered him before the throne; he was made Left Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuguo slandered him; he was made Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，蜀中亂，出為蜀州刺史，遷彭州。

translations.literal: Before long Shu rebelled and he was sent out as prefect of Shuzhou, then transferred to Pengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shu rebelled; he was Shuzhou prefect, then Pengzhou.

sentences.zh: 劍南自玄宗還京後，於梓、益二州各置一節度，百姓勞敝，適因出西山三城置戍，論之曰：

translations.literal: After Xuanzong returned to the capital Jiannan had a commissioner each at Zi and Yi; the people were worn out; Shi, because of garrisoning three western mountain cities, discussed it saying:
translations.idiomatic: After Xuanzong's return Zi and Yi each had a commissioner; the people were exhausted; Shi memorialized on western garrisons:

sentences.zh: 劍南雖名東西兩川，其實一道。

translations.literal: Though Jiannan is named Eastern and Western Two Rivers, it is really one circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Jiannan's two rivers are really one circuit.

sentences.zh: 自邛關、黎、雅，界於南蠻也；

translations.literal: From Qiong Pass, Li, and Ya it borders the southern barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: From Qiong Pass, Li, and Ya it borders southern tribes;

sentences.zh: 茂州而西，經羌中至平戎數城，界於吐蕃也。

translations.literal: west of Maozhou through Qiang lands to several Pingrong cities it borders Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: west of Maozhou through Qiang lands it borders Tibet.

sentences.zh: 臨邊小郡，各舉軍戎，並取給於劍南。

translations.literal: Small border prefectures each raise troops, all supplied from Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: Border counties raise troops all fed from Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 其運糧戍，以全蜀之力，兼山南佐之，而猶不舉。

translations.literal: Transporting grain and garrisoning takes all Shu strength with Shannan assisting, and still it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Supplying garrisons takes all Shu and Shannan—and still fails.

sentences.zh: 今梓、遂、果閬等八州分為東川節度，歲月之計，西川不可得而參也。

translations.literal: Now Zi, Sui, Guo, Lang, and five other prefectures form Eastern Chuan; in yearly accounts Western Chuan cannot be consulted.
translations.idiomatic: Eight prefectures now form Eastern Chuan; Western Chuan cannot share the accounts.

sentences.zh: 而嘉、陵比為夷獠所陷，今雖小定，瘡痍未平。

translations.literal: Jia and Ling were lately overrun by tribes; though slightly settled, wounds are not healed.
translations.idiomatic: Jia and Ling were ravaged; wounds remain.

sentences.zh: 又一年已來，耕織都廢，而衣食之業，皆貿易於成都，則其人不可得而役明矣。

translations.literal: For more than a year farming and weaving ceased and clothing and food are traded at Chengdu—so the people clearly cannot be levied.
translations.idiomatic: Farming ceased; Chengdu feeds them—levies are impossible.

sentences.zh: 今可稅賦者，成都、彭、蜀、漢州。

translations.literal: Now taxable prefectures are Chengdu, Peng, Shu, and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Only Chengdu, Peng, Shu, and Han can pay tax.

sentences.zh: 又以四州殘敝，當他十州之重役，其於終久，不亦至艱？

translations.literal: Four worn prefectures bear the corvée of ten—how hard in the long run?
translations.idiomatic: Four broken prefectures bear tenfold corvée—how long can that last?

sentences.zh: 又言利者穿鑿萬端，皆取之百姓；

translations.literal: Profit-seekers invent ten thousand schemes, all taken from the people;
translations.idiomatic: Profit-seekers invent schemes—all from the people;

sentences.zh: 應差科者，自朝至暮，案牘千重。

translations.literal: those liable for corvée from morning to evening face a thousand documents.
translations.idiomatic: corvée bearers face a thousand documents daily.

sentences.zh: 官吏相承，懼於罪譴，或責之於鄰保，或威之以杖罰。

translations.literal: Officials pass the blame, fearing punishment, charging neighbors or threatening with sticks.
translations.idiomatic: Officials fear punishment and squeeze neighbors or beat men.

sentences.zh: 督促不已，逋逃益滋，欲無流亡，理不可得。

translations.literal: Urging never stops and flight increases—no flightless peace is possible.
translations.idiomatic: Endless pressure breeds flight—peace is impossible.

sentences.zh: 比日關中米貴，而衣冠士庶，頗亦出城，山南、劍南，道路相望，村坊市肆，與蜀人雜居，其升合鬥儲，皆求於蜀人矣。

translations.literal: Lately Guanzhong grain is dear and gentry leave the city; Shannan and Jiannan roads are full; market towns mix with Shu people who sell every measure of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry flee dear Guanzhong to Shu, buying every grain measure there.

sentences.zh: 且田士疆界，蓋亦有涯；

translations.literal: Fields and soil have limits;
translations.idiomatic: Fields have limits;

sentences.zh: 賦稅差科，乃無涯矣。

translations.literal: tax and corvée have none.
translations.idiomatic: tax and corvée have none.

sentences.zh: 為蜀人之計，不亦難哉！

translations.literal: For Shu people's sake, is it not hard?
translations.idiomatic: For Shu, is it not hard?

sentences.zh: 今所界吐蕃城堡而疲於蜀人，不過平戎以西數城矣。

translations.literal: The Tibetan castles that weary Shu are only a few cities west of Pingrong.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan posts that weary Shu are only a few cities west of Pingrong.

sentences.zh: 邈在窮山之巔，垂於險絕之末，運糧於束馬之路，坐甲於無人之鄉。

translations.literal: Far on mountain peaks at utter precipices, grain is hauled on horse-binding roads and troops sit in empty land.
translations.idiomatic: Grain goes on deadly roads to empty peaks.

sentences.zh: 以戎狄言之，不足以利戎狄；

translations.literal: For the barbarians it does not profit the barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: It does not profit Tibet;

sentences.zh: 以國家言之，不足以廣土宇。

translations.literal: for the state it does not broaden territory.
translations.idiomatic: it does not broaden the realm.

sentences.zh: 奈何以險阻彈丸之地，而困於全蜀太平之人哉？

translations.literal: Why weary all peaceful Shu for a few perilous pinpoints?
translations.idiomatic: Why weary peaceful Shu for pinpoints?

sentences.zh: 恐非今日之急務也。

translations.literal: I fear it is not today's urgent task.
translations.idiomatic: It is not today's urgent task.

sentences.zh: 國家若將已戍之地不可廢，已鎮之兵不可收，當宜卻停東川，並力從事，猶恐狼狽，安可仰於成都、彭、漢、蜀四州哉！

translations.literal: If the state considers that already-garrisoned places cannot be abandoned and already-stationed troops cannot be withdrawn, then it should at least halt Eastern Chuan and combine its strength in the work; even then I fear distress. How can it rely on Chengdu, Peng, Han, and Shu prefectures alone?
translations.idiomatic: If the state considers that already-garrisoned places cannot be abandoned and already-stationed troops cannot be withdrawn, then it should at least halt Eastern Chuan and combine its strength; even then I fear distress. How can it rely on Chengdu, Peng, Han, and Shu prefectures alone?

sentences.zh: 慮乖聖朝洗蕩關東掃清逆亂之意也。

translations.literal: I fear this would run counter to the sacred court's intent to wash clean Guandong and sweep away rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: I fear this would run counter to the sacred court's intent to cleanse Guandong and sweep away rebellion.

sentences.zh: 倘蜀人復擾，豈不貽陛下之憂？

translations.literal: If Shu is disturbed again, will it not trouble Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: If Shu troubles again, will it not grieve Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 昔公孫弘願罷西南夷、臨海，專事朔方，賈捐之請棄珠崖以寧中土，讜言政本，匪一朝一夕。

translations.literal: Formerly Gongsun Hong wished to abandon the Southwestern Yi and Linhai and devote affairs solely to Shuofang; Jia Juanzhi requested abandoning Zhuya to pacify the central lands. Loyal words on the roots of government were not a matter of one morning and one evening.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Gongsun Hong wished to abandon the Southwestern Yi and Linhai and concentrate on Shuofang, while Jia Juanzhi requested abandoning Zhuya to secure the central lands. Forthright words on the roots of government were not a matter of one morning and one evening.

sentences.zh: 臣愚望罷東川節度，以一劍南，西山不急之城，稍以減削，則事無窮頓，庶免倒懸。

translations.literal: In my foolish view, I hope Eastern Chuan's military commission will be abolished, Jiannan made one, and the non-urgent western mountain cities gradually reduced; then affairs will not be exhausted without end, and perhaps the danger of hanging upside down can be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: In my foolish view, Eastern Chuan's military commission should be abolished, Jiannan made one, and the non-urgent western mountain posts gradually reduced. Then affairs will not be exhausted without end, and perhaps this upside-down peril can be avoided.

sentences.zh: 陛下若以微臣所陳有裨萬一，下宰相廷議，降公忠大臣定其損益，與劍南節度終始處置。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty finds my words one part in ten thousand useful, send down to the chancellery for loyal ministers to fix gain and loss with the Jiannan commissioner from start to finish.
translations.idiomatic: If useful, let the chancellery and Jiannan commissioner decide.

sentences.zh: 疏奏不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was rejected.

sentences.zh: 後梓州副使段子璋反，以兵攻東川節度使李奐，適率州兵從西川節度使崔光遠攻於璋，斬之。

translations.literal: Later Zizhou vice commissioner Duan Zizhang rebelled and attacked Eastern Chuan Commissioner Li Huan; Shi led prefectural troops with Western Chuan Commissioner Cui Guangyuan to attack Zhang and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Zizhang rebelled; Shi and Cui Guangyuan beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 西川牙將花驚定者，恃勇，既誅子璋，大掠東蜀。

translations.literal: Huajingding plundered Eastern Shu after killing Zizhang.
translations.idiomatic: Huajingding plundered Eastern Shu after killing Zizhang.

sentences.zh: 天子怒光遠不能戢軍，乃罷之，以適代光遠為成都尹、劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was angry Guangyuan could not restrain the army, removed him, and made Shi replace Guangyuan as Chengdu metropolitan governor and Western Chuan commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replaced Guangyuan with Shi as Chengdu governor and commissioner.

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，吐蕃陷隴右，漸逼京畿。

translations.literal: When Daizong took the throne Tibet took Longyou and pressed the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong's accession saw Tibet take Longyou and press the capital.

sentences.zh: 適練兵於蜀，臨吐蕃南境以牽制之，師出無功，而松、維等州尋為蕃兵所陷。

translations.literal: Shi trained troops in Shu on Tibet's southern border in order to contain them; the army went out without success, and Song, Wei, and other prefectures were soon captured by Tibetan troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shi trained troops in Shu on Tibet's southern border to contain them, but the campaign achieved nothing, and Song, Wei, and other prefectures soon fell to Tibetan troops.

sentences.zh: 代宗以黃門侍郎嚴武代還，用為刑部侍郎，轉散騎常侍，加銀青光祿大夫，進封渤海縣侯，食邑七百戶。

translations.literal: Daizong sent Yellow Gate Vice Director Yan Wu to replace him and bring him back; he was appointed Vice Minister of Punishments, then transferred to Regular Cavalier Attendant, given the rank of Silver-and-Blue Guanglu Grand Master, and advanced to Marquis of Bohai County with a fief of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong sent Yellow Gate Vice Director Yan Wu to replace him and bring him back. He was appointed Vice Minister of Punishments, then transferred to Regular Cavalier Attendant, given the rank of Silver-and-Blue Guanglu Grand Master, and advanced to Marquis of Bohai County with a fief of seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年正月卒，贈禮部尚書，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yongtai he died; posthumously Minister of Rites with posthumous name Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Yongtai 1, first month, he died; posthumously Minister of Rites, loyal.

sentences.zh: 適喜言王霸大略，務功名，尚節義。

translations.literal: Shi loved discussing hegemonic strategy, sought fame, and honored integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He loved grand strategy, fame, and integrity.

sentences.zh: 逢時多難，以安危為己任，然言過其術，為大臣所輕。

translations.literal: Meeting troubled times he took safety as his charge, yet his words exceeded his skill and great ministers slighted him.
translations.idiomatic: In crisis he took safety as his charge, but talk exceeded skill and ministers slighted him.

sentences.zh: 累為籓牧，政存寬簡，吏民便之。

translations.literal: Repeatedly a frontier governor, his rule was lenient and simple and officials and people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: As frontier governor he ruled leniently and people were at ease.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 其《與賀蘭進明書》，令疾救梁、宋，以親諸軍；

translations.literal: His "Letter to Helan Jinming" urged swift rescue of Liang and Song to reassure the armies;
translations.idiomatic: His letter to Helan Jinming urged rescuing Liang and Song to steady the armies;

sentences.zh: 《與許叔冀書》，綢繆繼好，使釋他憾，同援梁、宋；

translations.literal: his "Letter to Xu Shuji" carefully renewed friendship to dissolve old grudges and jointly aid Liang and Song;
translations.idiomatic: his letter to Xu Shuji sought to end old grudges and aid Liang and Song together;

sentences.zh: 《未過淮先與將校書》，使絕永王，各求自白，君子以為義而知變。

translations.literal: his "Letter to Officers Before Crossing the Huai" made them break with Prince Yong and each seek exoneration—gentlemen judged him righteous and knowing change.
translations.idiomatic: his letter before the Huai made officers break with Yong and seek pardon—men judged him righteous and adaptable.

sentences.zh: 而有唐已來，詩人之達者，唯適而已。

translations.literal: Among Tang poets who reached high office, only Shi did.
translations.idiomatic: Of Tang poets who reached high office, only Shi.

sentences.zh: 暢璀，河東人也。

translations.literal: Chang Cui was a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Cui was from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 鄉舉進士。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，安祿山奏為河北海運判官。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao An Lushan memorialized him as maritime transport judge of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tianbao Lushan made him Hebei maritime transport judge.

sentences.zh: 三遷大理評事，副元帥郭子儀辟為從事。

translations.literal: Three promotions to Dali judge; Vice Marshal Guo Ziyi made him an aide.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted thrice to Dali judge; Guo Ziyi made him aide.

sentences.zh: 至德初，肅宗即位，大收俊傑，或薦璀，召見悅之，拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide Suzong took the throne and gathered outstanding men; some recommended Cui; summoned and pleased, he was made remonstrating grandee.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong gathered talent, Cui was summoned, pleased, and made remonstrating grandee.

sentences.zh: 累轉吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年十二月，為散騎常侍、河中尹，兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Guangde he was Regular Attendant and metropolitan governor of Hezhong, also Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Guangde 2, twelfth month: Regular Attendant, Hezhong governor, Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，復為左常侍，與裴冕並集賢院待制。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he was again Left Regular Attendant and with Pei Mian served at the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Yongtai 1: Left Regular Attendant with Pei Mian at Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 大歷五年，兼判太常卿，遷戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dali he also judged the Director of the Court of Sacrifices and was transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Dali 5: judged Court of Sacrifices, then Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十年七月卒，贈太子太師。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the tenth year he died and was posthumously made Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Dali 10, seventh month, he died; posthumously Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 璀廓落有口才，好談王霸之略，居職責成屬吏。

translations.literal: Cui was open and had eloquence, loved discussing hegemonic strategy, and in office demanded results from subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Cui was open, eloquent, fond of strategy, and demanded results from staff.

sentences.zh: 齪齪無過而已。

translations.literal: He merely avoided fault.
translations.idiomatic: He merely avoided fault.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：祿山寇陷兩京，儒生士子，被脅從、懷茍且者多矣；

translations.literal: The historian says: When Lushan seized the two capitals, Confucian scholars and gentlemen who were coerced, clinging to expediency, were many;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: When Lushan took the capitals, many scholars clung to expediency;

sentences.zh: 去逆效順，毀家為國者少焉。

translations.literal: those who left rebellion for loyalty and ruined their households for the state were few.
translations.idiomatic: few ruined their households for loyalty.

sentences.zh: 如光遠勇決任氣，會權變以立功；

translations.literal: Such as Guangyuan, bold and headstrong, meeting crisis used opportunism to achieve merit;
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan used bold opportunism to win merit;

sentences.zh: 房琯文學致身，全節義以避寇。

translations.literal: Fang Guan rose by letters, kept integrity to avoid the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Guan rose by letters and kept integrity fleeing rebels.

sentences.zh: 阽危之時，顛沛之際，有足稱者。

translations.literal: In peril and hardship there was something to praise.
translations.idiomatic: In peril each had something to praise.

sentences.zh: 然光遠居重籓，掌軍政，琯登相位，奪將權，聚浮薄之徒，敗軍旅之事，不知機而固位，竟無德以自危。

translations.literal: Yet Guangyuan held a great fief and military power, Guan reached the chancellery and seized command, gathered frivolous men, and ruined the army—not knowing the moment yet holding position, in the end without virtue and in danger.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Guangyuan and Guan held power without skill and ruined armies.

sentences.zh: 孺復兇狂，式之便佞，獲令終者幸焉。

translations.literal: Rufu was vicious, Shi fawning—those who died in bed were lucky.
translations.idiomatic: Rufu was vicious; Shi fawning—lucky were those who died in bed.

sentences.zh: 鎬直躬居位，重德鎮時，其為人也鮮矣。

translations.literal: Gao was upright in office, heavy in virtue to steady the age—rare as a man.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was upright and rare.

sentences.zh: 適以詩人為戎帥，險難之際，名節不虧，君子哉！

translations.literal: Shi as poet became military commander; in hardship his name and integrity did not fail—a gentleman indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Shi the poet kept integrity in war—a gentleman!

sentences.zh: 璀擢第居官，守分無過，又何咎焉。

translations.literal: Cui passed examinations, held office, kept bounds without fault—what blame?
translations.idiomatic: Cui kept bounds without fault—what blame?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：光遠、房琯，有始有終。

translations.literal: The praise says: Guangyuan and Fang Guan had beginning and end.
translations.idiomatic: Praise: Guangyuan and Guan had beginning and end.

sentences.zh: 張鎬國器，適、璀儒風。

translations.literal: Zhang Gao was state vessel; Shi and Cui were Confucian wind.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was state vessel; Shi and Cui Confucian wind.
